definitions.explanation: A student who transfers into a school from another school, typically mid-year or at the start of a new term.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}から{転入生|てんにゅうせい}が{来|く}る。
examples.english: A transfer student is coming starting today.

examples.japanese: {転入生|てんにゅうせい}を{皆|みんな}の{前|まえ}で{紹介|しょうかい}した。
examples.english: The transfer student was introduced in front of everyone.

examples.japanese: {転入生|てんにゅうせい}はクラスにすぐ{馴染|なじ}んだ。
examples.english: The transfer student quickly fit in with the class.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}の{転勤|てんきん}で{転入生|てんにゅうせい}として{新|あたら}しい{学校|がっこう}に{通|かよ}うことになった。
examples.english: Because of my father's job transfer, I ended up attending a new school as a transfer student.

notes:
Composed of {転入|てんにゅう} (transfer in) + {生|せい} (student). A common trope in Japanese anime and manga is the mysterious or exciting {転入生|てんにゅうせい} who disrupts the classroom dynamic. In real life, transfer students are common in Japan due to the frequency of corporate relocations ({転勤|てんきん}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {転入生|てんにゅうせい}が{来|く}る: a transfer student arrives
- {転入生|てんにゅうせい}を{迎|むか}える: welcome a transfer student
- {転入生|てんにゅうせい}の{自己紹介|じこしょうかい}: transfer student's self-introduction
- {転入|てんにゅう}{手続|てつづ}き: transfer enrollment procedures

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {転校生|てんこうせい}: transfer student (more common in everyday speech)
- {編入生|へんにゅうせい}: student admitted mid-course (university level)
- {留学生|りゅうがくせい}: international/exchange student (different concept)
